title: Vector and Colony
premise: Ivo Iversen smuggles stolen memories in sealed neural wafers past the customs ring of Halcyon Station, and alone tends a deep-space beacon whose commissioning records have been erased. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, the beacon answers with a signal no human wrote: the colony ship Meridian, drifting dark for two centuries, is waking its cryo-banks — but only half the sleepers can be revived before power dies, and the selection protocol was written by Ivo's own forgotten ancestors. As factions on Halcyon fight over who deserves to wake, Ivo discovers their memory-smuggling career was itself an inheritance: every wafer they've carried contains fragments of the Meridian's true mission log. In the end, Ivo chooses truth over loyalty to their found family of smugglers, broadcasts the unedited log, and wakes neither faction's chosen half but the colonists' own elected council — accepting exile aboard the dying ship as it limps toward a world that may not forgive them.
about_author: P. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years maintaining automated beacons along the Norwegian coast before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about people who keep machines running for reasons no one remembers.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Establishes daily life: running contraband memories past orbital customs, then making the lonely pilgrimage to maintain a beacon with no paperwork, no owner, no history. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine competence; Ivo admits they keep the beacon out of something like love.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Mid-delivery, gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds. Cargo shatters, ships drift, and the beacon transmits for the first time in living memory. Emotional beat: vertigo and awe; the ordinary world revealed as fragile.

chapters.title: Customs Seal
chapters.summary: Inspector Vess Oka's POV. Customs locks down Halcyon Station, hunting whoever triggered the anomaly. She finds Ivo's beacon logs and realizes someone has been maintaining an unregistered transmitter for years. Emotional beat: professional suspicion curdling into personal obsession.

chapters.title: Wafers and Water
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Hiding at the smuggler enclave called the Drowned Deck, Ivo opens one of their own carried wafers and finds a fragment of the Meridian colony ship's mission log — footage of a launch two centuries old. Emotional beat: disorientation; the cargo was never contraband, it was a message.

chapters.title: The Meridian Answers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The beacon relays a decoded transmission: the Meridian, lost since launch, is alive in the outer dark, waking cryo-pods — but its reactor will fail before all sleepers can be revived. Emotional beat: collective shock giving way to immediate, ugly arithmetic.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Vess Oka's POV. Halcyon's governing families claim revival rights by charter; the dockworkers' syndicate claims them by labor; the Church of the Seeded Earth claims them by covenant. Oka sees the law fracturing. Emotional beat: dread of a war fought over sleeping bodies.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Smuggled
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following the wafer fragments, Ivo learns their grandmother was the Meridian's chief archivist who escaped the ship before it went dark — and seeded the system with memory-wafers containing the true crew manifest and election records. Emotional beat: grief and fury at an inheritance delivered as errands.

chapters.title: The Drowned Deck Splits
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Ivo's found family of smugglers fractures: some want to sell the manifest to the highest bidder, some want to destroy it, one — Ivo's partner Ryn — wants to wake only the engineers who could build them a future. Emotional beat: loyalty straining against truth.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Tea
chapters.summary: Vess Oka's POV. Oka brings Ivo in not with cuffs but with questions, revealing she has traced the beacon's maintenance back three generations of Iversens. She offers immunity for the manifest. Emotional beat: unexpected kinship between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: Cryo Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. Aboard a captured tug racing toward the Meridian, Ryn runs the numbers: the reactor dies in forty days; reviving anyone costs power needed to keep the rest alive. Every choice is murder deferred. Emotional beat: cold clarity hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Erased Commission
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Deep in Halcyon's founding archives, Ivo discovers the beacon wasn't anonymous — it was commissioned by the Meridian's planners as a lighthouse for their return, then deliberately struck from record when the first colony government betrayed the ship. Emotional beat: betrayal across generations; the lie is the colony's foundation.

chapters.title: Sabotage at the Ring
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The Church of the Seeded Earth bombs the relay array to prevent any 'impious' selection. Ivo and Oka, now uneasy allies, restore the link from the beacon itself. Emotional beat: improvised trust under fire.

chapters.title: Voices from the Dark
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Direct contact with the Meridian's caretaker AI, which has kept faith with its dead instructions for two hundred years. It asks Ivo, as archive-heir, to choose. Emotional beat: crushing weight of inherited authority.

chapters.title: Ryn's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. Ryn secretly offers the governing families the manifest in exchange for a guaranteed share of revival slots for the Drowned Deck. Emotional beat: love weaponized; betrayal framed as protection.

chapters.title: The Unedited Log
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Assembling all recovered wafers, Ivo reads the complete mission log: the sleepers themselves voted, before launch, on exactly this contingency — an elected council decides, not the colony left behind. Emotional beat: revelation as relief; the ancestors already answered.

chapters.title: Fleet of the Faithful
chapters.summary: Vess Oka's POV. All three factions launch armed ships toward the Meridian. Oka must choose between her oath to Halcyon and the evidence Ivo has shown her. Emotional beat: conscience over career.

chapters.title: Boarding the Meridian
chapters.summary: Ivo and Ryn's alternating POV. They board the dark ship through a hull wound two centuries old, walking corridors of frost and sleeping faces. Ryn confesses the bargain; Ivo must decide whether loyalty survives it. Emotional beat: heartbreak in a frozen cathedral.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds Again
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The Meridian's failing reactor triggers a second system-wide gravity stutter — the same signature as the first. Ivo realizes the original flicker was the AI's distress call, and the beacon has been screaming for help for two hundred years. Emotional beat: terrible understanding.

chapters.title: The Council Wakes
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Defying every faction, Ivo uses the last reactor margin to revive only the seven elected councilors named in the log. The factions' fleets arrive to find the decision already made — and made by the sleepers themselves. Emotional beat: defiant vindication shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: Reckoning at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Ivo and Ryn's POV. The governing families attempt to seize the ship; Oka turns her customs cutter between them and the airlock, citing the restored charter. Ryn takes a bullet meant for Ivo. Emotional beat: sacrifice settling debts loyalty couldn't pay.

chapters.title: Exile and Heading
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The council, awake and furious at everyone, sentences no one — instead offering Ivo passage as the ship's new archivist. Ivo accepts exile from Halcyon, leaving the beacon in Oka's hands. Emotional beat: bittersweet departure; home redefined as duty.

chapters.title: Vector and Colony
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ivo's POV. Months later, the Meridian burns toward a habitable moon while Ivo writes the true log into fresh wafers and scatters them ahead like seeds. The final line mirrors chapter one: another beacon, another reason nobody remembers yet. Emotional beat: inheritance continued, chosen this time.
